ip_top_stories.title: New York Times-Led Publishers Escalate Copyright Fight, Seek Court Sanctions Against OpenAI
ip_top_stories.summary: A coalition of news publishers led by the New York Times has filed for court sanctions against OpenAI, alleging the company withheld and concealed evidence in ongoing copyright litigation. The legal battle, which now reportedly exceeds $28 million in costs, centres on claims that OpenAI used publishers' copyrighted content without authorisation to train its AI models. Publishers are urging the court to penalise OpenAI for what they describe as an evidence cover-up.

ip_top_stories.title: AI companies want to water down Australia's copyright laws. Artists are outraged, Labor is split
ip_top_stories.summary: AI companies are lobbying Australian lawmakers to weaken copyright protections to permit training on copyrighted material, provoking a strong backlash from artists and creators. The issue has exposed divisions within the Labor government over how to balance AI industry interests against the rights of rights-holders. The story is reported against a broader backdrop of a tech giant also lobbying Australia's Treasurer Jim Chalmers for 'clarity' on AI copyright rules.

ip_top_stories.title: AI Music Training Hits Two Courts in July: Suno Faces Verdicts in Munich and Boston
ip_top_stories.summary: AI music generation company Suno is facing simultaneous legal proceedings in both a Munich court and in Boston during July, marking a significant escalation of copyright litigation against AI music training practices. The cases will test how courts in different jurisdictions treat the use of copyrighted music to train generative AI systems. The dual proceedings could produce divergent rulings with significant implications for the AI music industry.

ip_top_stories.title: Kenyan author who used AI loses copyright claim in landmark ruling
ip_top_stories.summary: A Kenyan author who used AI tools in the creation of their work has lost a copyright claim in what is being described as a landmark ruling. The decision reinforces the principle that AI-generated or AI-assisted content may not qualify for full copyright protection, with significant implications for creators who incorporate AI into their work.

ip_top_stories.title: Over 100 authors sue Anthropic for pirating books to train AI
ip_top_stories.summary: More than 100 authors have filed a lawsuit against Anthropic, alleging the AI company used pirated books without authorisation to train its AI models. The case adds to a growing wave of litigation from the creative community against AI developers over the use of copyrighted literary works in training data.

ip_further_links.title: Tech giant lobbied Chalmers for 'clarity' over AI copyright laws
ip_further_links.summary: A major technology company lobbied Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers seeking regulatory clarity over AI copyright laws, adding to pressure on the Australian government to reform its copyright framework.

ip_further_links.title: Can AI Copyright Tools Be Manipulated? Delhi High Court Examines Suit Against Meta
ip_further_links.summary: The Delhi High Court is examining a lawsuit against Meta that raises questions about whether AI copyright detection tools can be manipulated, with implications for how such tools are used as evidence in IP disputes.

ip_further_links.title: Midjourney Wants Hollywood to Reveal Its AI Use in 2026
ip_further_links.summary: AI image generator Midjourney is pushing for Hollywood productions to disclose their use of AI tools, raising questions about transparency, credit, and copyright in AI-assisted film and media production.

ip_further_links.title: OpenAI faces sanctions bid as copyright case escalates
ip_further_links.summary: OpenAI is facing a formal bid for court sanctions as its copyright case with news publishers escalates, with plaintiffs alleging the company failed to preserve and disclose relevant evidence.

ip_further_links.title: Google Accused Of Plundering Car Photos To Train AI Ad Tool
ip_further_links.summary: Google is facing accusations that it used car photographs without authorisation to train an AI advertising tool, in a case that highlights ongoing disputes over the scraping of images for commercial AI development.

ip_further_links.title: The NO FAKES Act Moves Forward: How AI Voice and Likeness Rights Could Reshape Entertainment Deals
ip_further_links.summary: The NO FAKES Act is advancing in the US, with proposed legislation that would create federal protections for individuals' voices and likenesses against unauthorised AI replication, potentially transforming how entertainment contracts are structured.

ip_further_links.title: AI Copyright Wars Shift To Main Street
ip_further_links.summary: Copyright disputes over AI training data are increasingly affecting smaller, everyday businesses and creators, not just large media organisations, as the legal and policy battles broaden in scope.

ip_further_links.title: PM to unveil AI agenda as government seeks to calm copyright concerns
ip_further_links.summary: Australia's Prime Minister is set to announce an AI policy agenda as the government attempts to address growing concerns from the creative sector over copyright and AI training data.

ip_further_links.title: Never Too Late: If you missed the IPKat last week!
ip_further_links.summary: IPKat's weekly roundup covers recent developments in intellectual property law, including AI and copyright-related cases and commentary from the past week.

ip_further_links.title: The government's secretive AI threat to creatives
ip_further_links.summary: A report examines government-level discussions around AI policy that could undermine copyright protections for creative professionals, raising concerns about transparency and the exclusion of creatives from the policy process.
